B_mechanism.note: genius heads propose a contiguous block; the verify ('reason over them') pass accepts a longest greedy-agreeing prefix plus one bonus token; outputs remain bit-identical to A

verdict: THEORY WORKS, SPEED NEUTRAL AT CURRENT FIRE RATE. (1) Compile: Qwen2.5-0.5B -> NCM genius weights (4 parallel multi-token heads, 168KB RAM-resident) compiled closed-form in 81.7s data->weights (87.1s incl. model load), bit-identical on recompile, single 460s slice. (2) Correctness: genius-block generation with the verify/reason pass is token-identical to autoregressive on 30/30 items (29/30) at equal strict accuracy 50.0% - acceptance 93.8% when fired, so multi-token blocks are genuinely usable. (3) Speed: 8.25 vs 8.35 tok/s = 0.988x (MARGINAL, not >= 1.10x): the frozen fire rule triggers on 5.3% of steps, so AR fallback dominates. (4) Removing the reasoning step (C) speeds nothing meaningful (1.016x) and costs 16.7pp accuracy (33.3% vs 50.0%) - 'generate many tokens together THEN reason over them' is the right architecture; trusting the genius block blind is not. HONEST BOTTOM LINE: the NCM mechanism is real and accuracy-safe; tok/s gain on CPU is currently ~1x because the confidence gate fires rarely. The lever for the big run is more probe data into the same closed-form compile plus higher digit-density answering format, not a protocol change.
honest_notes: S2 landed in the MARGINAL band: the frozen tau (60th pct of correct-case confidence on probe val) fires on only 5.3% of generation steps; acceptance when fired is 93.8% but the 2-forward cost of verify iterations roughly cancels the block savings at this fire rate on 2-thread CPU
C (trust genius block, no reasoning) is only 1.016x faster and loses 16.7pp strict accuracy: the 'reason over them' step is necessary and cheap
fires concentrate in numeric stretches of the CoT; verbose LaTeX style keeps digit-token density low, capping both fire rate and achievable block length

the big-run lever per this experiment: raise probe data volume and digit-token density (shorter-format exemplars) so the SAME closed-form compile fires more often at equal precision - no protocol change needed, only more data into weights
